messages.author: b4e76ba6d40254bf
messages.subject: Uploading a Text File
parts:
I see that people have successfully been able to upload .csv files, and I was able to get that sample code to work as well.  However, when I try to read in a text file that I have uploaded, I get the following error message:  "empty directory"

Here is my code and URL to illustrate the issue.  Please let me know if you see where I am going wrong.  I can read the metadata on the file, with the "output$fileInfo" function, but can't read in the file. Any thoughts for me?

http://glimmer.rstudio.com/moyoporter/upload_text/

#ui.R
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel("Upload a Text File"),
  
  sidebarPanel(    
    fileInput('file1', 'Upload a Text File (.txt)',
              accept=c('text', 'text/plain'))  
  ),  
    
  mainPanel(
    tableOutput("fileInfo"),   
    textOutput("inputUserText")
     )
 ))

#server.R

library(tm)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  
  readText <- reactive({
    
    inFile <- input$file1
    if (is.null(inFile))
      return(NULL)
    myCorpus <- Corpus(DirSource(inFile$datapath), readerControl = list(language = "eng"))
  })
  
  output$fileInfo <- renderTable({
  inFile <- input$file1
    if (is.null(inFile))
      return(NULL)
    inFile
  })
  
  output$inputUserText <- renderText({
    b <- readText()
    print(b[[1]])
  }) 
})


Thanks,
Ben

For others following this conversation, here is the version of readText() that works.  All of the rest of the code I posted earlier remains the same.  There is probably a more dynamic regex way to make sure that I am removing the file name rather than just ignoring the last character, but it works.

    inFile <- input$file1
    if (is.null(inFile))
      return(NULL)

upload.path <- substr(inFile$datapath,1,nchar(inFile$datapath)-1)
    myCorpus <- Corpus(DirSource(upload.path), readerControl = list(language = "eng"))
    
  })

Great! See basename/dirname functions. 


Also just be aware that the datapath file is in the temp dir for the whole R process. So depending on what Corpus/DirSource does, you may end up with files you didn't mean to (for example if two users are using the app simultaneously).
